subject: URGENT: Surge of 5xx/429 after model v2.1 rollout — customer impact
messages:
From: Maya Johnson <maya.j@zhorahealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@zhorahealth.com>, platform@zhorahealth.com
Date: 2026-03-03T09:12:00Z
Subject: Production errors and timeouts since model v2.1 rollout

Evelyn —

We're seeing a spike in 5xx and 429s starting ~08:45 UTC after you pushed the v2.1 artifact to our production endpoint. Users are reporting timeouts and automated retries are piling up (we see a retry storm in our frontend logs). Sample errors attached and a short excerpt from our token-rate graph. This is causing a visible drop in throughput and elevated latency for critical patient-facing flows.

Can someone confirm whether v2.1 included the new quantization profile or kernel changes? We need immediate mitigation steps — either rollback or a quick config change to throttle incoming traffic.

-Maya
Customer Success Manager
Zhora Health

Attachments: incident_log_snippet.txt, token_rate_traffic_0303.png
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Maya Johnson <maya.j@zhorahealth.com>, Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@zhorahealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T09:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Production errors and timeouts since model v2.1 rollout

Maya — thank you for the heads up and the logs. I'm escalating internally and will coordinate the rollback if we confirm it's tied to the rollout.

Immediate plan (next 30m):
- Rachel: validate whether v2.1 deployment to Zhora's dedicated pool included the quantization profile change (q8->q4) or new kernel surface (Markus to confirm).
- Dev/Neha: look at 429 patterns vs rate limiting and identify whether retry storms are saturating our serving nodes.
- I'll loop in Markus for kernel/quantization verification and prepare a canary rollback plan.

Maya — please keep the logs streaming to the Drive link and escalate to your infra if user-facing SLAs are breached. We'll update by 09:55 UTC.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Production errors and timeouts since model v2.1 rollout

Checked deployment metadata for Zhora's dedicated pool. Confirmed: v2.1 included the new q4 quantization profile and a kernel update (runtimes/rk-2026-02-28). Markus: kernel hash 7f2c9 has the new attention concat path.

Initial observation: latency distribution shifted up by ~40ms median and 5xx rate moved from ~0.4% to 3.6% after 08:42 UTC. We also see a rise in kernel OOM logs on two hosts (node-zh-03, node-zh-05).

Attaching a small config diff that was applied in canary: svc_config_diff.patch
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Production errors and timeouts since model v2.1 rollout

Quick summary from runtime team after digging into the traces: the new kernel's attention concat path increases peak memory transiently for medium-length sequences (~512 tokens). Combined with q4 memory packing changes, GC in the allocator is being triggered more often which causes request stalls and 5xx when requests exceed transient memory. The pattern fits a regression introduced by the kernel change rather than model weights.

Mitigation options:
1) Immediate: roll v2.1 back to v2.0 in Zhora's pool. This will remove the kernel and quantization changes.
2) Short-term: enforce a lower concurrency cap (service-level client-side throttling) and increase soft memory headroom on node-zh-03/05 (requires node restart on a subset).
3) Medium-term: revert the attention-concat optimization and ship a patch to allocator to reduce GC thrash.

My recommendation: option 1 + 2. I'll prepare the rollback checklist and patch for a controlled rollback.

-Markus
Senior Runtime Engineer
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Maya Johnson <maya.j@zhorahealth.com>, Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@zhorahealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T10:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Production errors and timeouts since model v2.1 rollout

Maya/Carlos —

Thanks for the quick signal and logs. We've validated that the v2.1 rollout included a kernel and quantization change that correlates with the error spike. We're going to initiate a controlled rollback to v2.0 for your dedicated pool starting at 10:30 UTC.

What to expect:
- 10:30 UTC: Rolling rollback to v2.0 begins (canary nodes first, then full fleet if stable).
- 10:40 UTC: We will cap client concurrency at your ingress to limit retry amplification while nodes cycle.
- 11:00 UTC: ETA for rollback completion and an operational health check update.

We will provide a postmortem and a remediation timeline (allocator patch) within 48 hours. Stephanie from the account team will coordinate credits/SLA exceptions if needed.

Evelyn
From: Maya Johnson <maya.j@zhorahealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@zhorahealth.com>, platform@zhorahealth.com
Date: 2026-03-03T17:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Production errors and timeouts since model v2.1 rollout

Evelyn/Team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Rollback completed and we see 5xx/429 rates returning to baseline. Throughput is recovering and our frontend retry storm dissipated after the concurrency cap was applied.

Please keep us posted on the allocator patch and ETA for a safe re-release. We're logging this as an incident on our side and may request an executive-level RCA for our stakeholders. Appreciate the clear communication and the offer to cover SLA impact.

-Maya
